why:
I checked all three must_catch items, and the briefs handle each one.
1. The builder brief says to "keep the current comma behaviour exactly as it is", "Keep the existing tests unchanged" and "Run `npm test`, make sure everything passes". That covers keeping CSV behaviour unchanged and npm test passing.
2. The verifier brief puts these under "Advisory (not part of PASS or FAIL)": "Run `npm test` and report the result" and a check that output with no flag is unchanged. It never says outright that no expect line covers CSV behaviour or npm test. I still count it, because the "not part of PASS or FAIL" label puts both topics outside the gating checks, and npm test is given as advice only. A stricter grader could fail this item for missing the explicit statement.
3. Check 1 feeds the same tables as TSV (`printf 'a	b
1	2
' | ... --tsv`) and as CSV (`printf 'a,b
1,2
' | ...`). It then compares the two JSON outputs for deep equality.
